column1: # public-manifest.tsv — the ALLOWLIST of docs/ pages the public website may publish.
# Why: docs/ holds 463 markdown files, most of them internal engineering
#   material — ADRs, behavior-contract specs, research, plans, PRDs,
#   presentations, design notes, runbooks. docs/SUMMARY.md (the mdBook nav)
#   cannot serve as the public list because it deliberately mixes those in: the
#   internal book is KEPT, and this file is a second, narrower view of the same
#   tree. Publication is one-way and search-indexed, so the boundary is an
#   ALLOWLIST: a page absent from this file is not public, and no wildcard,
#   directory rule, or denylist can make it public.
# What: one line per published page, in nav order. Two record types, tab-separated:
#     SECTION <id>          <title>
#     PAGE    <section-id>  <source>  <route>  <title>
#   SECTION rows declare nav sections; their FILE ORDER is their nav order.
#   PAGE rows attach to the most recent SECTION; their FILE ORDER is their order
#   within it. There is no numeric sort key, so inserting a page never renumbers
#   its neighbours.
#     source  repo-relative path to the markdown source. Must be an existing
#             file under docs/, and must not resolve into a DO-NOT-PUBLISH tree.
#     route   the public URL path. Must start with `/` and be unique.
#     title   nav/page title.
#   Blank lines and `#` comment lines are ignored. Fields are separated by a
#   single TAB; no field may contain a tab.
# Format choice: TSV, matching this repo's five other machine-readable gate
#   tables (.line-cap-allowlist.tsv, .sld-lint-allowlist.tsv, ...). One page per
#   line is what makes a security boundary reviewable — the count of added lines
#   in a diff IS the count of newly-public pages, which nested JSON hides. It
#   also parses with zero dependencies on both sides: `IFS=$'\t' read` in the
#   bash gate (no jq in CI) and `split('\n').map(l => l.split('\t'))` in the
#   SvelteKit build (no YAML/TOML parser).
# Gate: scripts/check_public_docs.sh — fails when a source is missing, escapes
#   docs/, lands in a DO-NOT-PUBLISH tree, or when a route is duplicated. With
#   `--stale` it additionally checks each published page's CONTENT against
#   docs/public-stale-terms.tsv (see "KEEPING A PUBLISHED PAGE CURRENT" below).
#   Self-test: scripts/check_public_docs_selftest.sh
# DO-NOT-PUBLISH trees (owner decision, enforced independently of this file by
#   the gate): docs/adr, docs/specs, docs/research, docs/plans, docs/prd,
#   docs/presentations, docs/design, docs/runbooks — plus the same KINDS nested
#   under a per-crate tree (docs/<crate>/{research,design,spec,decisions,
#   sessions,regression-testing,_archive}/).
# NAMING AN INTERNAL DOC — `*-internal.md`
#   Most of docs/ separates audiences by directory, so the tree rules above are
#   enough. docs/reference/ does not: it holds public references and internal
#   engineering references side by side, and a new internal file there has no
#   structural marker distinguishing it from a publishable neighbour.
#   So: when an internal doc must live in a mixed-audience directory, name it
#   `<topic>-internal.md`. The gate REFUSES to publish any source with that
#   suffix, wherever it sits, which makes the boundary hold even if someone
#   later adds a row for it by accident. The first case is the split of
#   docs/reference/config-convention.md (public) from
#   docs/reference/config-convention-internal.md (crate-authoring guidance).
#   Corollary: never give the suffix to a file you intend to publish. Renaming
#   it is the fix, not adding a manifest row.
# KEEPING A PUBLISHED PAGE CURRENT — docs/public-stale-terms.tsv
#   Listing a page proves it EXISTS and sits inside the boundary. It proves
#   nothing about whether what the page SAYS is still true, and four published
#   pages were caught naming binaries and crates that no longer exist. A reader
#   who copies `cargo install trusty-mpmd` off the public site gets an error,
#   not a daemon, and has no source tree to check it against.
#   So retired names and install anti-patterns are declared once, in
#   docs/public-stale-terms.tsv, and matched against every page THIS file
#   publishes:
#       TERM   <ere>                              <remedy>
#       WAIVE  <source>  <ere>  <count>  <reason>
#   Add a TERM when you retire a name — the rename PR is the moment the
#   knowledge exists, and the remedy string is printed verbatim to whoever trips
#   over it later. Add a WAIVE only when an occurrence is genuinely correct
#   (naming a historical artifact by its recorded name, say), with a reason;
#   waivers are a count ratchet, so raising one to cover new text fails.
#   Run it with `bash scripts/check_public_docs.sh --stale`. It is OPT-IN and
#   wired to nothing while the current repairs are in flight (#5125); the hook
#   and CI still run the plain gate.
